what: PDF to JPG turns every page of a PDF into a picture. You can choose JPG or PNG and pick the resolution. When it finishes, you see a small preview of each page, and you can save single pages or download all of them in one ZIP file.
Use it when you want to post a page on social media, put a slide into a presentation, send a page in a chat app that does not show PDFs, or use a page in a design or photo editor.
The pages are drawn by your browser with the pdf.js library. The PDF is not uploaded.
uses: Share a page in a chat app
Messaging apps show pictures instantly, while PDFs must be opened. Send a page as a JPG instead.
Insert a chart or table from a PDF report into a presentation as an image.
Turn a flyer or poster PDF into an image you can upload.
Create preview images of a document for a website or catalog.
Edit a page as a picture
Open the image in a photo editor to crop, annotate or highlight part of a page.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop a PDF here" or drag a PDF onto the box. The tool shows the file name and size.
"JPG" makes smaller files and suits photos and most pages. "PNG" keeps text and lines perfectly sharp but files are larger.

"Standard (72 dpi)" draws each page at its normal screen size and gives the smallest files. "High (144 dpi)" doubles the width and height and is the default. "Very high (216 dpi)" triples them, which is good for printing or zooming.
The tool shows "Converting page 2 of 8…" as it works. A preview of each page appears below as soon as it is ready, with a caption like "Page 2 · 312 KB".
Click or tap any preview to save just that page. Files are named like report-page-2.jpg.
Click "Download all (ZIP)" to get one ZIP file, named like report-images.zip, that holds every page image.
features: Choose small JPG files or sharp PNG files.
72, 144 or 216 dpi, so you can pick between small files and fine detail.
See each page as it is converted, with its file size.
Tap a single preview to save it, or download every page together in a ZIP.
Each image is named after the PDF and its page number.
Convert documents of up to 200 pages in one go.

example.title: Worked example: a one-page flyer for social media
example.text: Sara has event-flyer.pdf, one A4 page. A4 is about 595 x 842 points, so at "High (144 dpi)" the image is twice that: about 1191 x 1684 pixels. She keeps "JPG", clicks "Convert to images", and sees one preview with a caption like "Page 1 · 420 KB". She taps the preview to save event-flyer-page-1.jpg and posts it.

tips: For pages with mostly text, PNG at High often looks cleaner than JPG.
For a quick preview to send in a chat, Standard and JPG give the smallest files.
If you only need a few pages, use Split PDF first to make a smaller PDF, then convert it.
Very high resolution makes large files. Use it only when you need to print or zoom in.
To turn images back into a PDF later, use JPG to PDF.
problems: The message says the PDF has more than 200 pages
Use Split PDF to extract the pages you need, then convert the smaller file.
A message says a page "is too large for this resolution"
The page is very big, such as a poster or drawing. Choose a lower resolution and try again.
Choose "Very high (216 dpi)" or switch to PNG, then convert again.
A message says the file "is password protected"
Remove the password in a PDF reader that knows it, save a copy, and use that copy.
